subject: pol-con
title: POL.CON. ------SOC.RT.
description: Diagram in AE(PD)-6 (Aspect Essence / Perception Dynamics, Level One) accompanying Braxton's diagnostic of the move toward non-functionalism: 'I believe that the move towards non-functionalism in the seventies is directly related to the realness of both spectacle diversion progressionalism … as well as the aspect-essence distortions which came to permeate composite information dissemination.' POL-CON (political concept) is crossed with SOC-RT (social reality): the question is what political-concept produces when crossed with social-reality — under conditions where aspect-essence distortions have come to permeate information dissemination. INFO-INTR (information interior) and SOC-RT cluster in the upper register. (R)INTR (the reality of interior) feeds into the central axis from the upper-left. CRTF-D (creative-dynamic) anchors the upper-right output. RT-DYM (reality dynamics) feeds upward into the subject from below-left. POL-P (political particulars) sits between subject and partner on the central axis. SPT-DYM (spectacle dynamics) hangs on the right output. MT-INFO (multi-information) anchors the right margin. INFO-F (information functionalism) sits below. C-CONT (composite continuance) anchors the lower-right. Structural argument: political-concept crossed with social-reality is mediated by political-particulars as central hub, with the reality-of-interior as upper upstream and reality-dynamics as lower upstream. The presence of spectacle-dynamics in the right output cluster is load-bearing: it exposes that political-particulars under these conditions produces *spectacle-dynamics* as an output (not as an input as in earlier diagrams) — Braxton's structural diagnostic that the seventies' non-functionalism is the consequence of political-particulars *itself* generating spectacle, rather than spectacle being imposed externally.
